chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him.' He said: 'It expiates from his sins to the extent of what he forgives.'

And I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'But if any remission is made to any one by his (aggrieved) brother, then prosecution (for the blood wit) should be made according to usage, and payment should be made to him in a good manner.' He said: 'It is befitting for the one who has the right that he should not constrain his brother when he has reconciled with him upon the wergild, and it is befitting for the one upon whom is the right that he should not delay his brother when he has the ability to give what he owes, and he should pay it to him in a good manner.'

He said: 'And I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever exceeds the limit after this, he shall have a painful punishment.' He said: 'He is the man who accepts the wergild, or forgives, or reconciles, then exceeds, so he kills. Thus, for him is a painful punishment, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says.'
ai.seo_question: How does forgiving a financial or bodily right expiate sins according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual and social dimensions of blood money (diyah) and forgiveness, linking the expiation of sins directly to the magnitude of one's graciousness. He establishes a reciprocal ethical framework where the creditor avoids hardship and the debtor fulfills obligations with excellence, warning that exceeding these bounds after reconciliation incurs divine punishment. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence) in interpersonal justice as a means of spiritual purification.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:45] but he who foregoes it, it shall be an expiation for him. So heasws said: ‘It would expiate from his sins by the measurement of what he forgave’. And I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:178] but if any remission is made to any one by his (aggrieved) brother then prosecution (for the blood wit) should be made according to usage, and payment should be made to him in a good manner. Heasws said: ‘It is befitting for the one for whom is the right that he should not (financially) constrain his brother when he has reconciled with him upon the wergild, and if it befitting for the one upon whom is the (payable) right that he should not delay his brother when he has the ability upon what he has to be given, and he should pay it to him in a good manner’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:178] so whoever exceeds the limit after this he shall have a painful Punishment. So heasws said: ‘He is the man who accepts the wergild, or forgives, or reconciles, then exceeds, so he kills. Thus, for him is the painful Punishment just as Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says’.
